caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 325 of 1976 with Civil Rule No. 1174 (S) of 1975.
lawyer:
Md. Ansar Ali ------ For the Appellant. 
Akram Hossain Amin ------ For the Respondent.
parties:
Jasimuddin Mondal and ors------Appellants.
Vs.
Sunila Bibi and others------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
This appeal at the instance of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is directed against a judgment of affirmance in a suit for partition on declaration of plaintiff's title to the extent of ten annas ten gonads share in the lands described in schedules 1 to 3 And 5 to 12 and fourteen annas share in the land of schedule 4 and for recovery of khas possession and in the alternative, joint possession if the plaintiff is not found to be entitled to khas possession on partition by metes and bounds. 

 "That the suit be decreed in the preliminary form on contest with cost against decants. 1 and 2 and exparte against the rest without' cost Puff's title in her 10 annas and 10 gondas and In 14 annas share in the lands in schedules Nos. 1-3 and 5-12 and in schedules. No. 4 respectively to the plaint be hereby declared. PM's, do get a separate Sahara for her share in the suit lands by partition by metes and bounds. She does get khas possession thereon by evicting the Defdts therefrom. On partition Defdts. 1 and 2 also do get a separate saham for their 4 annas share in the lands in schedule Nos. 1-3 and 7-12 by partition by metes and bounds. 

 "In reaching this conclusion the learned Munsif decided all the issues raised in the suit. According to the learned Munsif, all the properties held jointly by the parties have been brought into hotchpotch after amendment of the plaint on remand. The learned Munsif held that the suit was not bad for defect of parties and all the Persons interested in the disputed properties have been impleaded in the suit. Turning to the question of plaintiff's title to the suit land, the learned Munsif held that the plaintiff has ten annas ten gondas share in lands of schedules 1-3 and 5-12 by inheritance. The learned Munsif further' found that Jamiruddin had sixteen annas share in the land of schedule 4. According to the learned Munsif, the defendant No. I deposed in the suit as D.W. 4 and he admitted in his reposition that the plaintiff has acquired  share claimed by her in the suit land. The learned Munsif granted separate saham in favour of defendant No.1 and 2. In view of the finding on the question of plaintiff's title, the learned Munsif granted a decree for partition holding that the plain-tiff is entitled, to get separate saham in her share by metes and bounds and khas possession in the lands allotted to her on partition.
